Murali Maddula | Metabolic Health Advocate on Instagram: "White Rice + Rajma Curry… does adding protein and fiber automatically mean a smaller glucose spike? 👀
Rajma brings fiber and plant protein to the plate, but it brings carbohydrates too! Based on portion estimates, this meal of 200g cooked Sona Masuri rice + 200g rajma curry contained approximately 90g of total carbohydrates.
Fiber and protein can influence digestion and glucose absorption, but they don’t cancel out carbohydrates. Food pairing matters and so does portion size.
My CGM recorded a 44-point rise, with a relatively quick climb, a rounded top and a sharp drop. The graph alone cannot tell us how much the fiber or protein helped.
Next experiment: the same meal with two teaspoons of pure cow ghee + two boiled eggs. Will the rise be smaller, will the peak happen later, or will the response stay similar? We’ll examine the full curve!
Watch till the end and share with a rajma-chawal lover! 
Experiment & Disclaimer: I am not diabetic, and this personal experiment is for educational purposes only, not medical advice. CGM readings reflect my response to this particular meal; individual responses can vary. Nutrition figures are estimates and depend on the rice, curry recipe, bean-to-gravy proportion and actual serving. A single glucose curve cannot establish whether a meal is healthy or suitable for everyone.

Dr. Rhonda Patrick on Instagram: "Eating blueberries improves vascular function.

One cup per day is effective, but half a cup does not not produce the same benefit.

Adults with metabolic syndrome that ate one cup rather than only a half-cup or matched placebo improved flow-mediated dilation (FMD) by about 1.5 percentage points in a six-month randomized trial.

FMD measures how effectively an artery widens when blood flow increases, essentially a “stress test” for the endothelium. It’s relevant because studies have shown it is a strong predictor of future cardiovascular disease events.

The one-cup dose is consistent with other studies showing cardiovascular, metabolic, and brain-health benefits of blueberries.

My latest solo episode explores the wide-ranging health benefits of blueberries. Watch or listen now on YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Podcasts."

Andrew Huberman, Ph.D. on Instagram: "ENTRAINMENT GOVERNS YOUR ENERGY & FOCUS •

Entrainment is one of the most powerful aspects of our biology. 

Our circadian rhythm is created within us, but numerous studies show that our health is best when it is entrained to the rising and setting of the sun. That’s not to say you have to wake up at sunrise, but people who try to live nocturnally definitely suffer health consequences and people who match their sleep rhythm even somewhat to the rising and setting of the sun (one form of entrainment), derive many health benefits.

Entrainment works on shorter time scales too. Exercise at roughly the same time for a few days and you’ll notice your energy will increases a few minutes before that typical workout time.

Study or do some reading or some other form of work or learning at roughly the same time or times per day, and you’ll notice that your mental sharpness will start to increase in anticipation of those times.

To be clear, some of this is psychological, but a lot of it is physiological. The neuromodulators, hormones and neurotransmitters that regulate alertness and focus are readily susceptible to entrainment.

And entrainment is a concept that we can leverage. Not to make us rigid, but understanding it can help you make better sense of why you are more energetic and mentally sharp at particular times of day, and it can give you flexibility over what those times are.
